Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:142176

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 30830 of 2023

Applicant :- Manoj Sahani
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Kshitiswar Nath Yadav,Dinesh Chandra Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.

1. Heard Sri Kshitiswar Nath Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Kunwar Tejendra Bahadur, learned AGA for the State-respondent.
2.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
058 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Chitaipur,
District Varanasi, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his mother and according to the FIR,
marriage of the applicant was performed with the deceased about four years before and after marriage, applicant and his mother harassed the deceased for Rs. Two lacs and on 31.5.2022, they have committed her murder.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the entire allegations made against the applicant are totally false and baseless and applicant neither harassed the deceased nor he ever demanded any dowry and only being husband he has been made accused in the present matter.

He further submitted that although in the autopsy report of the deceased, cause of death has been mentioned as smothering but actually deceased was suffering from chronic disease of asthama and high blood pressure and on the date of incident, she suffered serious attacks of asthama and died.
6.

He further submitted that mother in law of the applicant has already been released on bail by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order date 21.12.2022 passed in Crl. Misc. Bail Application No.
48913 of 2022 and applicant is in jail in the present matter since 2.6.2022 i.e. for almost a year.

sentences.text:
7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within four years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home and post mortem report suggests that it is a case of homicidal death,
therefore, applicant should not be released on bail.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. Although, mother in law of the deceased has been released on bail but applicant is husband and post mortem of the deceased shows that his wife died due to smothering, therefore, prima facie, it appears that it is a case of homicidal death.

10. Although, in the instant bail application in paragraph-23 of the affidavit, it is averred that deceased was suffering from chronic disease of asthama and high blood pressure, therefore,
possibility cannot be ruled out that she might have suffered severe attacks of asthama and died but in the light of autopsy report of the deceased, defence taken by the applicant cannot be appreciated,
at this stage.
11. Applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died in her matrimonial home within four years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry.

12. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
13. Accordingly, the instant bail application stands rejected.

14. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
